_readme: WHICH ROWS A REPO REBUILD GIVES BACK, AND WHICH ONLY A BACKUP HAS.
tests/schema-drift.mjs proves the repo rebuilds the SCHEMA and says so in its
own header: 'DATA. This proves the SCHEMA rebuilds. It says nothing about
whether any row survives a restore.' This file is the other half.
Every base table in public carries a `class`:
seeded           the repo reconstructs the rows; no backup needed. `replay` is
PINNED, so a catalogue that would rebuild to a different size
fails the guard instead of quietly running a different game.
restore_only     the repo creates the table EMPTY. Only a backup has the rows.
This is the data-loss surface, and it is what the runbook is
for. `wiped_at_cutover` is REQUIRED and says whether losing it
before the cutover would have cost anything.
operational      accumulates from the database simply running. Losing it costs
observability history, never player value. Not asserted.
regenerated      rebuilds to the right COUNT and the WRONG VALUE, on every
apply. Exactly one table: hr_server_secrets.
operator_tunable one authored row seeded `on conflict do nothing` that an
OPERATOR is expected to change at runtime. A rebuild restores
the AUTHORED DEFAULT and silently reverts the live value.
`live_value` is REQUIRED: it is what a rebuild re-applies from.
Two manifests make the classifications un-downgradeable:
player_value_tables   tables whose class may not be anything but restore_only.
player_value_exempt   every OTHER table carrying a user_id, each with a written
reason for why losing every player's rows costs nothing.
A new player-scoped table that appears in neither fails the build.
Regenerate replay figures with `node tests/restore-census.mjs --write`.
Classifications are AUTHORED, never generated — deciding what a restore owes
a table is a judgement, and --write preserves whatever is already here.

method: Read-only. `select count(*)` over every base table in public, in one
statement built from pg_class, executed against the live database. Not
reltuples — reltuples was wrong on two tables at this size (bug_reports
estimated 21, actual 27; maintenance_log estimated 51, actual 106), which
is the whole reason this block records exact counts.
_what_changed_since_2026_08_15: THE CUTOVER HAS HAPPENED AND THIS BLOCK IS NO LONGER HYPOTHETICAL.
inventory rows, 79 equipment rows, 119 farm plots, 914 progress rows and
12,301 ledger rows. Every one of those is restore_only — a repo rebuild
returns them EMPTY. There is no client-side copy any more (server authority
is live and game_saves is never read), so the sentence 'the database is the
only copy of every player's progression' stopped being a forecast on this

backups.data_loss_window: UP TO 24 HOURS. The newest backup was 11h07m old at measurement; every character-hour since then existed in exactly one place. PITR is a separate paid add-on and is OFF — enabling it takes the window from ~24h to minutes.
_recommendation: ENABLE PITR. The census now measures 35 live characters and 12,301 ledger
rows with no second copy anywhere. A daily-only backup accepts losing an
entire evening of everyone's progression to one bad migration or one
corruption event, and that loss is not recoverable afterwards because the
ledger is the only record of what was earned. This is a durability
recommendation, not an upsell: the free tier had NO backups at all, Pro
fixed that, and PITR is the one remaining gap between 'we lose a day' and
SECOND, AND FREE: RUN THE DRILL. restore_drill.last_executed is null.
Eight backups that have never been restored are eight rumours.

_why: The disk fills on the FILESYSTEM number, not on pg_database_size. 34 MB of
database sits on a filesystem holding 330 MiB (WAL, catalog, logs). Plan
capacity against fs_used_bytes.
Measured via GET /v1/projects/{ref}/config/disk and /config/disk/util.
disk.autoscale_policy: none configured (growth_percent, min_increment_gb, max_size_gb all null) — platform default applies
projection: At 49 accounts / 35 characters the whole database is 34 MB and the
filesystem is 16.7% used. The two tables that scale with PLAY (not with
signups) are player_ledger and hr_combat_xp_credit_log, and both have
retention: hr-ledger-prune (hourly, 20k rows, 90-day window from
hr_ledger_config) and hr-combat-xp-credit-prune (nightly, 1 day). Linear in
characters at fixed retention:
10x  (350 characters):   ~62 MB ledger, ~16 MB credit log, ~0.4 GB fs
100x (3,500 characters): ~620 MB ledger, ~160 MB credit log, ~2.1 GB fs
So the 2 GB disk is the binding storage constraint at roughly 100x — not the
old 500 MB free-tier database limit, which no longer applies on Pro, and not
compute. Disk is resizable and the number to watch is fs_used_bytes, which
hr_db_samples now records hourly so growth is a trend rather than a
surprise.
CONNECTIONS BIND FIRST. max_connections is 60 with 22 in use at 35
characters; the same measurement was 25-in-use at six players on 2026-08-15,
so the floor is mostly platform overhead and the per-player slope is
shallow — but Edge Functions open a connection per invocation and the
failure at exhaustion is TOTAL (nobody connects, dashboard included). The
hard rule is unchanged: all Edge traffic through the transaction-mode
pooler on 6543. See docs/design/server-authority.md §2a-ii.

_why: Measured 2026-08-30 by comparing the production counts above against what
the migration chain rebuilds (the `replay` pins below). A SEEDED table that
differs is a live content divergence: production's players earned their rows
against production's catalogue, and a rebuild would hand them a different
game. This block RECORDS AN OPEN ISSUE — it is not an acceptance. The
--live-compare mode reports it every time it is run until it is closed.
Everything not listed here matched exactly (515 items, 473 activities, 275
item slots, 142 unlock offers, 108 bounty monsters, 72 RPC baseline rows,
34 castle items, 28 feast foods, 19 goal rewards, 17 skills, 17 companion
grants, 13 combat styles, 9 crops, 6 hunt bosses, 5 tiers, 3 runes, 2
traits …).

hr_unlocks.delta_is_entirely_in: namespace='companion' — production has 4, a rebuild produces 21
hr_unlocks.meaning: The companion unlock generation in the repo has not reached production. A rebuild would ship 17 companion unlocks production has never had, and a restore planned against the repo's catalogue would be planned against the wrong game.
hr_unlocks.owner: Backend Architect — this is an apply-state question, not a DR one. Reliability records it so that a restore is never planned against the wrong catalogue.

_why: NOT asserted by the guard and NOT reconstructible from this repository.
Recorded because the runbook needs it and because auth.users is the single
most important table in the system that no migration creates.
_auth_users_is_the_root: 17 foreign keys in public reference auth.users, 12 of them ON DELETE
If auth.users is empty, none of the player rows can even be INSERTED back,
and every player has lost their account. It is carried by a Supabase
backup restore (the clone feature lists 'Auth user data' explicitly) and by
NOTHING in this repository. Re-measured 2026-08-30: 49 accounts.
_schema_migrations_is_stale_and_that_is_: while the repo grew past a hundred migration files, because migrations here
are applied by hand through execute_sql rather than by the CLI. Consequence
for DR: that table CANNOT be used to answer 'which migrations does
production have'. tests/schema-drift.mjs --live-sql is the authority for
that question, and this census's divergence_vs_repo block is the row-count
_storage_is_not_in_any_backup: Supabase documents that database backups do NOT include objects stored via
the Storage API — the database holds only metadata. One bucket, eleven
objects at measurement (was one on 2026-08-15). Nothing player-facing
depends on it today; if that ever changes, Storage needs its own backup and
this line must stop being true.

how_to_remeasure: node tests/restore-census.mjs --live-sql   -> read-only SQL; paste into the
Supabase SQL editor or the MCP execute_sql tool, save the rows as JSON.
Backup state, also read-only, via the Management API:

_why: A rebuilt database that comes back without its retention jobs is a disk
with a fuse on it. game_events reached 1,598,269 rows / 229 MB from six
players in four days — 94% of a 244 MB database — and the fix was a
retention job. The guard pins every job the chain schedules by name,
schedule AND command, so a rebuild silently losing one fails the build.
Twelve here + hearthrise-leaderboards below = production's thirteen,
verified against cron.job 2026-08-30.
expected: trim-chat-messages | 15 3 * * * | delete from public.chat_messages where created_at < now() - interval '60 days'
_retention_is_a_budget_ledger_here: TWO of these jobs prune tables that are ALSO day-ceiling ledgers:
The daily cap is `sum(applied)` over the log, so a prune that runs with too
SHORT an interval does not merely lose history — it resets a character's day
ceiling mid-day and re-mints a full day of credit. 2026-09-01 raised the kill
prune's floor from 1 hour to 2 days for exactly that reason. Do not 'tidy up'
either interval without reading the cap query it feeds.

hearthrise-leaderboards: PRODUCTION HAS IT (jobid 6, '*/5 * * * *',
'select public.hr_leaderboard_refresh(true)', re-verified 2026-08-30) and
the chain DOES schedule it on a real Postgres. The PGlite replay cannot see
it, for a structural reason worth writing down rather than working around:
2026-08-08-leaderboards.sql is the ONLY file that opens its cron block with
`create extension if not exists pg_cron`, inside a nested handler whose
`exception when others` does `return`. PGlite has no pg_cron extension — the
fixture supplies a cron SCHEMA and shim functions, not the extension — so
the create raises, the handler returns out of the whole DO block, and the
schedule never runs. Every other file guards with to_regclass('cron.job') /
to_regprocedure('cron.schedule(text,text,text)'), which the shim satisfies.
PROVEN BY EXECUTION, not by reading: replaying the chain with that single
line elided produces 'hearthrise-leaderboards' and replaying it unchanged
does not. So this is a stand-in artefact, NOT a hole in the rebuild.
Consequence for the guard: it covers 12 of production's 13 jobs. It is not
listed in `expected` because a guard must not assert what it cannot observe,
and it is written down here so that '12 jobs OK' is never read as '13
covered'. --live-compare knows about this exemption by name.
VERIFY THE THIRTEENTH BY HAND after any real rebuild:
select jobname, schedule from cron.job order by jobname;   -- expect 13

_why: tests/sql/pglite-fixture.sql pre-schedules these two so that market-v2's
unschedule has a real pre-state to act on. No migration in the chain creates
them and production does not have them (both were disarmed —
trim-expired-listings would DESTROY escrowed goods under market v2). They
are subtracted before comparison. A rebuild does NOT resurrect them.
An untested backup is a rumour. This census proves which rows a restore
must carry. It does not prove Supabase gives them back — only executing the
runbook against a real restore target does that. Set `last_executed` to the
date it was run and record the measured RTO here and in the runbook.
ONLY A REAL DRILL MAY SET THIS FIELD. It is not a checkbox: the census
prints 'RESTORE DRILL: NEVER EXECUTED' in a banner at the top of every
single run, before any other output, on the passing path as well as the
failing one, precisely so the absence cannot be lived with comfortably.
As of 2026-08-30 there are eight daily backups on Pro carrying 35
characters' entire progression and not one of them has ever been opened.

_player_value_tables_why: THE CLASS OF THESE IS NOT NEGOTIABLE: restore_only, always. They hold a
player's earned progression, their escrowed or banked goods, their claimed
identity, or a budget ledger whose loss RE-MINTS value rather than losing it.
The realistic way this guard dies is not deletion — it is somebody turning a
red build green by editing one word, moving player_state to 'operational'.
This manifest makes that a separate, visible, argued change: the guard fails
with 'PLAYER-VALUE TABLE DOWNGRADED' and says the removal must happen here,
in the same commit, with a reason.
The two non-obvious members are the credit logs. hr_combat_xp_credit_log and
hr_kill_credit_log look like idempotency scratch — the same shape as
player_intents, which IS exempt — but the daily ceiling is `sum(applied)`
hands every character a second full day of combat XP and kill credit. That is
the player_ledger lesson repeated on two newer tables, and it is why 'it is
only an idempotency log' is the wrong reading.

player_value_exempt.beta_signup_log: Append-only signup audit: outcome, normalised code, ip, email domain. Enforced append-only like player_ledger. It carries no player VALUE — a lost row costs a player nothing — but it is the abuse-forensics record behind the invite gate, so losing it costs the ability to answer 'who burned this code and from where'. Diagnostic, not restorative.
player_value_exempt.bug_reports: 51 rows of player-submitted support history with screenshots. Real diagnostic value, zero player value: nothing a player earned is in here, and a lost report costs a triage thread rather than progression.
player_value_exempt.clan_bans: Clan moderation state — who a clan has barred. Officer-recreatable in one action, and empty in production. Losing it un-bans someone, which is a moderation redo rather than a value loss.
player_value_exempt.clan_invites: Transient outstanding clan invitations, empty in production. Re-issuable by any officer in one click; a lost invite costs a click.
player_value_exempt.game_events: Telemetry, 7-day retention (trim-game-events). Reached 1,598,269 rows / 229 MB — 94% of a 244 MB database — before the retention job; 352 rows at the last measurement. Zero player value; total loss acceptable at any moment.
player_value_exempt.game_saves: The RETIRED client-authored blob. server-authority.md §2a-iv is explicit — 'Starting state is FRESH. game_saves.snapshot is never read' — so post-cutover a restore has no reason to bring it back, and reading it would launder the forged values the audit found. One row survives as an artefact. Exempt because restoring it is not merely unnecessary, it is forbidden.
player_value_exempt.hr_import_marker: Operator bookkeeping for the one-time cutover import: which snapshot sha was imported for which character, what was written and what was refused. Six rows. The VALUE it describes landed in player_state/inventory/skills, which are all on the manifest; this is the audit of that event, not the event. Still classified restore_only, because an irreplaceable record of an irreversible action deserves a backup — but 'it holds a player's stuff' is not why it matters.
player_value_exempt.hr_rate_counters: Unlogged rate-limit counters, 1,012 rows. Losing them resets every rate window to EMPTY — the correct failure direction (permissive for one window, never denying a legitimate call) and self-healing within a minute. UNLOGGED tables do not survive a crash by design, so depending on them would already be a bug.
player_value_exempt.hr_rejections: Sampled hr_apply rejections, pruned nightly. Anomaly-detection history only: it records that a call was refused, never that anyone was owed anything.
player_value_exempt.player_intents: The 24-hour idempotency window, pruned hourly by hr-intents-prune. Losing it means a retry INSIDE the window is no longer deduplicated — bounded by the version and watermark checks hr_apply makes anyway. Deliberately contrasted with the two credit logs, which look identical and are not: no ceiling is summed over this table.
player_value_exempt.player_ledger_rollup: Aggregates written by hr_ledger_prune as it deletes aged ledger rows. Derived — but NOT re-derivable once the source rows are pruned. Losing it loses history beyond the 90-day ledger window; it is never read to decide a live value, so no player is poorer for its loss.
player_value_exempt.session_claims: Single-active-session heartbeat rows keyed on the browser TAB. Self-healing: a lost claim is re-taken on the next heartbeat, and save-invariant #2 means absence can never evict anyone (eviction requires a definitive fresh-heartbeat row, and no row is not that).

active_bounty.note: PLAYER VALUE. The bounty a character has ACCEPTED, with its target, required count, baseline, tier and the gold/marks/XP it will pay on completion — one row per character, 10 in production. Losing it does not merely reset a task: `baseline` is the kill count progress is measured FROM, so a player mid-bounty loses the work already done and the reward they were owed. Written only by the bounty RPCs (SECURITY DEFINER); no client write policy.

beta_invites.note: 30 codes with used_by/used_at. The CODES are operator-recreatable in one INSERT; the record of WHICH are burned is not, so a restore-free rebuild re-opens every spent invite. Low value, cheap to accept.

beta_signup_log.note: Append-only signup audit (63 rows): outcome, normalised code, user_id where an account actually resulted, ip, email domain. Enforced append-only by trigger — UPDATE and TRUNCATE always refused, DELETE only for aged rows — so it is the forensic record behind the invite gate and its throttle. No player value; losing it costs the ability to answer 'who burned this code, from where, how fast' after an abuse report. restore_only rather than operational because a security audit trail a rebuild silently empties is not observability, it is evidence.

bug_reports.note: 51 rows of player-submitted support history. No player value at stake, real diagnostic value. Survivable loss; not worth a decision at 3am.

chat_blocks.note: Per-player mute list. Empty today. Losing it silently un-mutes someone a player chose to block — small, but it is a player-authored safety setting, not telemetry.

chat_messages.note: 60-day retention job already trims this. Loss is acceptable at any time; nothing is derived from it.

clan_bans.note: Clan moderation state — who a clan has barred. Officer-recreatable, empty in production. Clan surface — see clans.

clan_board.note: The clan's own message board: player-authored text, no economic value. Clan surface — see clans.

clan_invites.note: Transient outstanding clan invitations, re-issuable in one click. Clan surface — see clans.

clan_ledger.note: Append-only clan journal AND the budget source for clan_deposit's per-day clamps, the same shape as player_ledger. Losing it resets every member's daily deposit ceiling to zero-used. Clan surface — see clans.

clan_members.note: Who is in which clan, at what rank, with what contribution standing — the record a clan's whole social state rests on. Clan surface — see clans.

clan_order_ballots.note: Clan governance ballots: the record of what a clan voted to build, and the input a work order is authorised by. Clan surface — see clans.

clan_order_votes.note: Individual votes cast on a clan order ballot; losing them loses the mandate behind a decision. Clan surface — see clans.

clan_raids.note: Raid instances and their progress — an in-flight raid is real elapsed effort. Clan surface — see clans.

clan_stores.note: The clan's shared bank: one row per item, holding goods members really deposited out of their own inventories. Clan surface — see clans.

clan_tavern.note: Clan tavern state — active feasts and the buffs they are paying out. Clan surface — see clans.

clan_withdrawals.note: The withdrawal journal behind the per-member per-day clamp. Losing it re-opens every member's daily withdrawal allowance against the clan bank. Clan surface — see clans.

clan_work_labour.note: Per-member labour contributed to a clan work order — the record of who actually did the work the reward is split by. Clan surface — see clans.

clan_work_orders.note: Open clan work orders and their accumulated progress. Clan surface — see clans.

clans.note: ⚠ DECISION NOT RECORDED ANYWHERE. CLAUDE.md says 'the beta WILL BE WIPED at cutover' with no carve-outs, and clan standing is derived from contributions earned in the wiped client-authored economy — so `true` is the defensible reading and is what is written here. But the clan/raid/world surface was built server-authoritative FROM THE START (docs/design/server-authority.md §2), which makes it the one part of the beta that was never exploitable, and nobody has written down whether it is in or out of the wipe. Owner: Tyler + Backend Architect. NOTE 2026-08-30: production now holds ZERO clans and zero members, so the question is academic for today's data — but the classification still governs any future restore and the ruling is still unwritten.

display_names.note: The uniqueness ledger behind 2026-08-08-unique-names.sql, 37 rows. This is IDENTITY, not progression: a wipe of progress does not take a player's name. Losing it frees every claimed name for re-registration by someone else, which is unrecoverable once a stranger takes it. Treat as must-restore.

game_events.note: Telemetry, 7-day retention (trim-game-events). Reached 1,598,269 rows / 229 MB — 94% of a 244 MB database — before the retention job and truncate brought it down; 352 rows at the 2026-08-30 measurement, which is the retention job doing its job. Zero player value; total loss acceptable. It is in this census only so the retention job that keeps it small stays pinned.

game_saves.note: The RETIRED client-authored blob: gold, inventory, every skill's XP, equipment, farm. One row left in production. server-authority.md §2a-iv is explicit — 'Starting state is FRESH. game_saves.snapshot is never read' — so a post-cutover restore has NO reason to bring it back, and reading it would launder the forged values the audit found. This is the single table whose value flipped from critical to worthless the moment the cutover completed, and the cutover has now completed.

hr_activities.note: Generated from src/data/*.js by tools/gen-catalogues.mjs; content guarded by --check as a smoke preflight. 344 rows on 2026-08-15, 473 now. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_bounty_monsters.note: Generated catalogue (2026-08-23-bounty-monsters.generated.sql, tools/gen-bounty-monsters.mjs --check, a smoke preflight): which monsters a cull bounty may target, at which tier. Server-owned reference data — a stale copy credits a bounty at the wrong tier's reward, which is why the generator has its own --check. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_castle_board_tasks.note: Hand-seeded by 2026-08-08-clan-seat-2.sql: the castle board task definitions. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_castle_buildings.note: Hand-seeded by 2026-08-08-clan-seat.sql: the castle building definitions and their costs. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_castle_items.note: Hand-maintained, seeded 'from src/data/items.js' BY COMMENT ONLY — server-authority.md §3.4 records it as the one catalogue tools/gen-catalogues.mjs does not own. Its migration DOES self-check, but asymmetrically: `if v_n < 34` is a FLOOR, so a catalogue that shrinks fails the migration and a catalogue that GROWS applies clean. The exact count pinned here is the only guard covering the second direction — proven by the shrink/grow mutation pair in tests/restore-census.mjs, which are caught by different mechanisms on purpose.

hr_castle_tiers.note: Hand-seeded by 2026-08-08-clan-seat.sql: the castle tier thresholds. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_catalogue_meta.note: The catalogue digest row — the generator's own fingerprint, written `on conflict do update` so the repo always wins and a rebuild is always self-consistent. Rebuilt from repo.

hr_client_rpc_baseline.note: The approved client-callable RPC list: 51 rows on 2026-08-15, 72 now. hr_assert_grant_hygiene check (2) raises on any grant not recorded here, nightly on cron. A rebuild that seeded a different set would make that detector wrong in both directions — silently permitting an unreviewed grant, or crying about a reviewed one.

hr_client_write_baseline.note: The register of KNOWN-WEAK client write grants awaiting a sweep. 2026-08-16-client-write-grant-sweep.sql inserts 21; sweeps 2, 3 and 4 delete each row as the grant behind it is revoked, so the chain ends — and production sits — at ZERO. Pinned at 0 deliberately: this is the one seeded table whose CORRECT value is empty, and a future migration re-registering a weak grant makes the census go red so somebody has to look at it rather than at a green tick.

hr_combat_styles.note: Hand-seeded by 2026-08-24-combat-style.sql: the combat style -> skill routing table (Attack/Strength/Defence/Ranged/Magic and the shared splits). Server-owned, and the client holds the same numbers — the live 'Defensive XP routed to Attack' bug was exactly a divergence between the two copies, so a rebuild producing a different set silently mis-routes every point of combat XP. Content additionally guarded by tests/combat-style.mjs. Rebuilt from repo.

hr_combat_xp_credit_log.note: PLAYER VALUE — AND A BUDGET LEDGER, which is why it is not 'just an idempotency log'. One row per credited combat-XP claim (user, slot, idem, claimed, credit, applied, throttled); 5,666 rows / 1.6 MB in production sixteen days after it shipped. 2026-08-31-combat-xp-credit.sql:253 reads `select coalesce(sum(applied),0) … from hr_combat_xp_credit_log` to compute the DAY CEILING, so restoring player_state without this table hands every character a second full day of combat XP — the player_ledger failure repeated on a newer table. Pruned nightly by hr-combat-xp-credit-prune at a 1-day floor. Restore it WITH player_state or not at all.

hr_companion_grants.note: Hand-seeded allowlist catalogue (2026-08-22-companion-grant.sql) mapping each companion to how it may be obtained (drop/skill/quest) and the item required. It is the SECURITY GATE for companion grants — a client cannot name a companion that is not here — so a rebuild producing a different set widens or narrows what can be granted. Scoped delete+insert, so re-applying re-syncs. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_crop_plot_tier.note: Generated farm catalogue (2026-08-22-farm-catalogues.generated.sql, tools/gen-farm-catalogues.mjs --check): which crops each plot tier is allowed to grow. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_crops.note: Generated catalogue — crop growth times and yields, the numbers every harvest is priced by. Content guarded by tools/gen-catalogues.mjs --check. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_db_samples.note: Hourly capacity telemetry taken by hr_cron_health: db_bytes, max/used connections, the top-N tables by size, and the set of ACTIVE cron job names at that instant. Four rows in production (sampling began 2026-08-30 18:44). It is the ONLY series that can answer 'has this job been known for more than 48 hours' for a job that has never produced a run row, and it is how disk growth becomes a trend instead of a surprise. Losing it loses the history, never a live value — the next sample is an hour away. It deliberately uses estimates (pg_class / pg_stat_all_tables) rather than count(*), because an exact count on the table you are watching is the one query guaranteed to hurt.

hr_equip_slots.note: Generated catalogue — the legal equipment slots every equip is validated against. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_farm_yield_perk.note: Generated farm catalogue (tools/gen-farm-catalogues.mjs --check): the farm-yield perk ladder. A stale copy silently changes every harvest, which is why the generator's --check gates the build. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_feast_foods.note: Hand-seeded by 2026-08-27-clan-economy-sinks.sql: which foods a clan feast accepts and what each contributes. It prices a clan-wide sink, so a rebuild with a different set changes what a feast costs a clan. Content drift is separately guarded by tests/clan-feast-catalogue-drift.mjs. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_goal_rewards.note: Hand-seeded by 2026-08-23-modal-goal-claims.sql: the SERVER's copy of every daily/weekly goal — counter kind, counter key, target, and the gold/gems/xp/items it pays. This is the PAYOUT table; the client renders it but does not author it. A rebuild producing a different set pays different rewards than the ones players' progress was earned against. RLS on with no policy — read by SECURITY DEFINER claim RPCs only. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_hunt_boss_reward.note: Generated catalogue (2026-08-22-raid-boss-rewards.generated.sql, tools/gen-raid-boss-rewards.mjs --check): the per-boss reward table for hunts. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_hunt_bosses.note: Hand-seeded by 2026-08-08-hunt.sql: the hunt boss definitions. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_hunt_tiers.note: Hand-seeded by 2026-08-08-hunt.sql: the hunt tier thresholds. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_import_marker.note: The cutover-import receipt: which snapshot sha was imported for which (user, slot), when, by which tool build, and a `counts` jsonb of what was written and what was refused. Six rows — six real characters imported once, irreversibly. Not player value in itself (the value landed in player_state / inventory / skills), but it is the ONLY record of what happened to a given player's stuff during a one-time irreversible event, and its own migration states the point is that 'what happened to my stuff' stays answerable a year later without the tool's output file. A rebuild returns it empty and that answer is gone permanently.

hr_item_slots.note: Generated catalogue — which items may occupy which equipment slot. 222 rows on 2026-08-15, 275 now. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_items.note: Generated catalogue — the market tradeable allowlist and every item's server-side truth. 426 rows on 2026-08-15, 515 now. Content digest guarded by tools/gen-catalogues.mjs --check as a smoke preflight.

hr_kill_credit_log.note: PLAYER VALUE — AND A BUDGET LEDGER. One row per credited kill claim (user, slot, idem, target, claimed, credit, cap, applied); 549 rows in production. 2026-09-01-kill-daily-credit.sql:658 reads `sum(applied)` over it for the DAY CEILING, and that file calls it 'the clan_deposit budget pattern' in as many words. Restoring player_state without it re-opens a full day of kill credit for every character. Its prune floor was raised from 1 hour to 2 DAYS in the same file for exactly this reason — a short prune resets a live budget mid-day. Restore it WITH player_state or not at all.

hr_ledger_config.note: The ledger retention window hr_ledger_prune enforces. Seeded `insert … values (true) on conflict do nothing` (2026-08-11-player-state.sql:446), so the row is created with the column DEFAULT and a rebuild can never reproduce an operator's change. retain_days is the single number deciding how much of the append-only audit trail exists at all — shortening it destroys history permanently, lengthening it is the largest single driver of disk (player_ledger is already the biggest table in the database). It matches its default today; the class records the mechanism, not the coincidence.

hr_market_config.note: The single-row market tuning table: house tax in basis points, listing TTL, per-seller listing cap, per-listing qty ceiling, and the per-trade GROSS ceiling that makes the overflow argument a bound rather than a hope. Seeded `on conflict do nothing` (2026-08-17-market-v2.sql:547), so a rebuild restores the AUTHORED DEFAULTS and silently reverts any live economy tuning. All six columns match their defaults today; the class records the mechanism, and the recorded live_value is what a rebuild re-applies from.

hr_plot_tier.note: Generated farm catalogue (tools/gen-farm-catalogues.mjs --check): the farm plot tier ladder and its unlock costs. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_rate_counters.note: Unlogged rate-limit counters. 1,012 in production, 9 in a rebuild (the migrations' own self-checks spend budget). Losing them resets every rate window to empty — the correct failure direction, and self-healing within a minute. UNLOGGED means they do not survive a crash by design, so nothing may depend on them.

hr_rejections.note: Sampled hr_apply rejections, pruned nightly by hr-rejections-prune. 128 rows. Anomaly-detection history only: it records that a call was refused, never that anyone was owed anything.

hr_runes.note: Generated catalogue (2026-08-11-catalogue.generated.sql, tools/gen-catalogues.mjs --check): the rune definitions the enchant path validates against. Three rows — small, but it is an ALLOWLIST, so a rebuild with a different set changes what may legally be enchanted. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_server_secrets.note: A REBUILD PRODUCES ONE ROW WITH A DIFFERENT VALUE. 2026-08-11-player-state.sql seeds it with sha256(gen_random_uuid()||gen_random_uuid()||clock_timestamp()), so the 256-bit PRNG secret is FRESH on every apply. A count-based census reports this table as reconstructed; it is not. What changes if the value changes: (1) hr_seed's accrual PRNG re-rolls, so a disputed drop can no longer be replayed deterministically from player_ledger — the stated reason the seed is deterministic at all; (2) the accrual idempotency key hr_seed(user,slot,'intent:accrue:<watermark>') moves, so an in-flight accrual retried across the boundary is no longer deduplicated and can pay twice — bounded, because accrued_to is restored with it and hr_apply re-validates against the restored watermark. Neither is fatal. Both are silent. A restore from a BACKUP keeps the real value; only a repo rebuild re-rolls it.

hr_settings.note: ⚠ THIS TABLE HOLDS A SECURITY SWITCH. `beta_gate` decides whether an invite code is REQUIRED to create an account; hr_beta_gate_is_open() reads it on every signup. It is seeded 'off' with `on conflict (key) do nothing` (2026-08-23-open-beta.sql:232), so a rebuild restores 'off' — OPEN SIGNUP — regardless of what an operator has since set, and the revert is completely silent. If the gate is ever closed in anger (an abuse wave, a spam run), a rebuild re-opens it. The live value at the last measurement is recorded here precisely so a rebuild has something to re-apply from; re-measure it with --live-sql BEFORE any rebuild, not after.

hr_skills.note: Generated catalogue — the skill list every XP write is validated against. 15 rows on 2026-08-15, 17 now. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_start_equipment.note: Generated from src/data/start-kit.js. A divergence here means server-created characters start with different gear than the client shows — a live bug this file's guard chain already caught once (0 gold, no weapon, into server-side combat).

hr_start_inventory.note: Generated from src/data/start-kit.js — the items a fresh character is created holding. Three rows on 2026-08-15, four now. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_start_kit.note: Generated from src/data/start-kit.js — starting gold and plot count for a fresh character. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_start_skill_xp.note: Generated from src/data/start-kit.js — the XP a fresh character starts each skill at. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_traits.note: Hand-seeded by 2026-08-23-trait-buy.sql: the SERVER's copy of the trait shop — id, name, currency (marks|gold), cost, prerequisite. It is the PRICE the server charges, and the client keeps its own copy in legacy.js TRAITS, so a divergence means a player is charged one price and shown another. Two rows today; content is separately guarded by tests/trait-buy.mjs. RLS on with no policy — read by SECURITY DEFINER only. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_unlock_offers.note: Generated catalogue (2026-08-16-unlock-offers.generated.sql, tools/gen-unlock-offers.mjs --check as a smoke preflight): every purchasable unlock offer with its namespace, rung and price. 142 rows, and it is a PRICE LIST — a rebuild producing a different set sells different things at different prices than the ledger's recorded purchases were made at. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

hr_unlocks.note: Generated unlock catalogue (2026-08-16-unlocks.generated.sql, by tools/gen-unlocks.mjs --check): merge rule, storage kind, ceiling, rung ladder per namespace. Rebuilt from repo, never restored. ⚠ PRODUCTION RUNS 65 AND A REBUILD PRODUCES 82 — see production.divergence_vs_repo; the whole delta is namespace='companion' (4 vs 21) and it is an apply-state issue, not a DR one.

hr_xp_table.note: The XP curve, 99 levels, with three anchor assertions in the migration. Every level in the game is derived from it. Rebuilt from repo, never restored.

leaderboard_meta.note: Board namespace metadata plus the refresh bookmark, seeded (1, now()) `on conflict do nothing` — a rebuild stamps its own refresh time, which hr_leaderboard_refresh overwrites within five minutes, so the divergence is self-healing and does not warrant operator_tunable. The board itself, leaderboard_ranked, is a MATERIALIZED VIEW — derived, not stored, and recomputed by hr_leaderboard_refresh; it is correctly absent from this census.

maintenance_alerts.note: hr_cron_health output, 16 rows. Losing it loses alert HISTORY, not the alerts — the next hourly run re-detects anything still wrong.

maintenance_log.note: Retention and cron run log. 478 rows in production, 3 in a rebuild. It is how 'did the prune actually run last night' is answerable; losing it costs that answer for the past, never for the future.

market_buy_offers.note: Legacy market buy offers. 2026-08-17-market-v2.sql drops and recreates the market tables; the old economy was discarded at cutover by design. Empty in production.

market_listings.note: ⚠ UNDER MARKET V2 A LISTING ROW *IS* THE SELLER'S ESCROWED GOODS — the items left the seller's inventory to create it. Empty in production at the 2026-08-30 measurement, which is the only reason this is not already a top-priority restore target. The moment it is non-empty, losing it destroys real player property with no second copy anywhere, and wiped_at_cutover=true stops being the right reading. REVISIT this classification the first time the market carries live listings.

market_sales.note: Completed market sales, 3 rows: the receipt both parties see and the only record of what a trade actually moved. Pruned by hr-market-sales-prune.

player_bank.note: PLAYER VALUE — the character's BANK, one row per item stack, qty > 0 enforced (a stack that reaches zero is DELETEd, so an absent row is a real zero). Written ONLY by hr_bank_move (SECURITY DEFINER); no client write policy. Empty in production today only because the bank shipped 2026-08-27 and players have not filled it — it is the same class of object as player_inventory, and a rebuild returns it EMPTY. It went days with NO DR classification at all while every other player_* table was classified, which is exactly the gap this census exists to close.

player_equipment.note: PLAYER VALUE. What each character is wearing — 79 rows in production. Equipping is a TRANSFER (the unit leaves player_inventory to get here), so losing this table does not merely unequip everyone: it destroys the items outright, because there is no other row holding them.

player_farm.note: PLAYER VALUE. One row per plot: crop, planted_at, watered_at. 119 rows in production. Readiness is derived from now() against planted_at, so losing the row loses the growing crop AND the seed that was spent to plant it.

player_intents.note: 24-hour idempotency window, pruned hourly by hr-intents-prune. 1,297 rows / 1.16 MB. Losing it means a retry inside the window is no longer deduplicated — bounded by the same version/watermark checks hr_apply already makes. Deliberately contrasted with hr_kill_credit_log and hr_combat_xp_credit_log, which look identical and are NOT operational: a daily ceiling is summed over those two and over none of this one.

player_inventory.note: PLAYER VALUE. One row per item; the bank cap is count(*) over it. 316 rows in production. A repo rebuild returns it empty and every player is holding nothing.

player_ledger.residue_note: A rebuild leaves exactly THREE orphan rows, and they are not player data. Three migration self-checks (2026-08-20-bestiary.sql, 2026-08-21-collection.sql and one sibling) call hr_create_character for a synthetic uuid to exercise a projection, then delete the player_progress, player_state and auth.users rows they created. They CANNOT delete the ledger row: hr_ledger_immutable refuses an in-window DELETE, which is precisely the property that makes the journal trustworthy. PRODUCTION HAS ZERO SUCH ROWS — verified 2026-08-30, `select count(*) from player_ledger where user_id::text like '00000000-0000-4000-c000-%'` = 0, hr_ledger_prune having aged them out — so this is a REBUILD artefact only. The count is pinned EXACTLY rather than tolerated as 'a few': the whole value of the restore_only=0 rule is that a migration which starts writing REAL player rows at apply time goes red. Suggested fix (Backend Architect, not blocking): wrap each self-check's writes in a nested BEGIN/EXCEPTION subtransaction and raise at the end, so nothing commits.
player_ledger.note: PLAYER VALUE AND THE AUDIT TRAIL. 12,301 rows / 6.2 MB in production — the largest table in the database. Append-only by trigger (UPDATE, TRUNCATE and in-window DELETE all refused), 90-day window from hr_ledger_config, pruned hourly with a rollup. It is the source of every daily budget: hr_day_budget_used SUMS this table rather than reading a counter, so restoring player_state WITHOUT player_ledger silently resets every player's daily gold/XP/item ceiling to zero-used — a restore that grants a second full day of budget. It is also the only record of WHY a player has what they have, which is the whole of dispute resolution. Restore the two together or not at all.

player_ledger_rollup.note: Aggregates written by hr_ledger_prune as it deletes aged ledger rows. Derived — but NOT re-derivable once the source rows are pruned. Losing it loses history beyond the ledger window, never live state. Empty today because nothing has aged past 90 days yet.

player_progress.note: PLAYER VALUE — quests, dailies, bounties, lifetime stats, collections, flags, and the bestiary kill counts. 914 rows in production. A generic (kind, key, period_key) -> value space; losing it resets every quest, every collection and every lifetime counter, and because the quest model is a LIFETIME count there is nothing else in the database it could be reconstructed from.

player_skills.note: PLAYER VALUE — XP per skill, the value every level and every leaderboard score is derived from. 595 rows across 35 characters. This is the single table a player would describe as 'my account'. A repo rebuild returns it empty.

player_state.note: PLAYER VALUE — gold, gems, hearth_tokens, hp, the activity pointer, accrued_to, version. 35 rows / 376 kB. THE row every write locks. Since the cutover this table has no second copy anywhere in the world: there is no client blob to fall back on, by design (server-authority.md §2a-iv).

player_workers.note: PLAYER VALUE — the character's hired crew: each worker's stable uid, name, assigned skill and gather target, its own XP, its fractional tick carry (acc_ms) and when it was hired. Six rows across six characters in production. Workers are BOUGHT (an unlock purchase) and then LEVELLED, so a lost row is both spent currency and accumulated progress; the acc_ms carry means even a mid-tick restore has a right answer to give. Written only by hr_worker_hire / hr_worker_assign / hr_apply; no client write policy. Like player_bank it shipped with no DR classification, which is the gap this census closes.

profiles.note: IDENTITY, not progression: the display name derived server-side for chat and the market. 49 rows. Losing it makes every player 'Adventurer' and breaks name authority until each player re-registers a name.

raid_claims.note: The once-only record that a raid reward has been collected — its entire purpose is to make a reward unclaimable twice, so losing it RE-OPENS every past claim and mints the rewards a second time. Empty in production, so nothing is at stake right now. Clan surface — see clans.

raid_contributions.note: Per-member contribution to a raid — the input the reward band is computed from, i.e. the record of work actually done. Empty in production. Clan surface — see clans.

session_claims.note: Single-active-session heartbeat rows, keyed on the tab. 34 rows. Self-healing: a lost claim is re-taken on the next heartbeat. Losing them cannot lock a player out (save-invariant #2 — eviction requires a definitive fresh-heartbeat row, and absence is not that).

world_event_joins.note: Which players joined a world event — the participation record a payout is gated on, so losing it either denies a share or re-opens one. World-event surface, same open wipe decision as clans.

world_event_pledges.note: What each player pledged to a world event: real goods or gold that moved out of their account to get here. World-event surface, same open wipe decision as clans.

world_event_totals.note: The aggregate progress of each world event. Derived from pledges in principle, but not re-derivable once pledges age out. World-event surface, same open wipe decision as clans.
